column11: derived: Merck generated $39,599mm of free cash flow on $189,294mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 20.92% margin, against the 29.5% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Solved so the modelled book reproduces that margin rather than assumed from one line's cost structure: the alliance rows carry no cost of sales and Animal Health carries its own, so a ratio taken off a single product does not reconcile the company. Restated before interest: MRK paid $3,700mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.95% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 12.10% to 10.14%. Restated at replacement capex: MRK spent $11,347mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $6,977mm of plant depreciation, 2.31% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 10.14% to 7.48%. Restated without one-off cash: MRK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $8,300mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $572mm of legal settlements; $1,200mm of US transition tax (2025 instalment 1,200mm). None recurs, so the charge falls from 7.48% to 2.06%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 MRK's cash flow statement shows receivables up $2,482mm, inventories up $2,831mm, payables down $88mm, a working capital build of $5,401mm, 2.85% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 2.06% to -1.23%. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3610 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.3746 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is -1.3576%.

column12: NOT THIS TRIAL'S OWN CRITERIA, and the gap is larger than on DII235. NCT07614984 requires only 'Has Lp(a) >= 150 nmol/L' and 'Is receiving an optimized and stable dose of statin for >= 30 days'; it names no atherosclerotic disease requirement at all, where DII235's NCT07235046 enrols Lp(a) of at least 150 nmol/L WITH ASCVD or type 2 diabetes. Two unsourced narrowings pull the other way and neither is cut: the 150 nmol/L entry threshold is higher than the 50 mg/dL the pool is drawn at, and no free US distribution of Lp(a) above 150 nmol/L in the general adult population could be found; and statin treatment is required, which NHANES would size but which I did not source. Against that, the row would be too low if a primary-prevention label follows, which is what lepodisiran.csv's wider 0.12 allows for

column11: held level with nvs_dii235.csv, the book's other Phase 2 claimant on this descriptor, which takes one third of the 0.06 the olpasiran and lepodisiran seeds carry. That 0.06 is Leqvio's measured uptake, the closest analogue on file, an injectable lipid agent into the same prescriber base: CMS Part B beneficiaries 6,779 in 2022, 24,690 in 2023, 48,298 in 2024, and worldwide revenue $355mm, $754mm, $1,198mm. The third is taken because the mechanism's one Phase 3 outcome trial has failed: nvs_pelacarsen.csv records that Lp(a)HORIZON missed its MACE endpoint on 2026-09-04 (Novartis 6-K 0001171843-26-005896), and that the 0.06 'was already a stretch on its own anchor, since Leqvio's measured 2024 capture was 27,659 new starts against the 288,337 that 6% of the elevated-Lp(a) pool implies'
column12: a judgement, and holding it level with DII235 is deliberate so the two Phase 2 Lp(a) assets filed under this descriptor sit on one footing rather than each claiming its own share of a pool the engine cannot ration. Case for higher: MK-7262 is oral and co-administered with enlicitide, Merck's oral PCSK9, where every other Lp(a) agent in the book is injected, and oral dosing is what turned statins into primary prevention. It also reads out in 2027 against DII235's 2037, so it would reach an emptier market. Case for lower: the mechanism's only outcome trial missed, and payers restrict biomarker-only lipid labels

column11: Leqvio, the closest analogue on file, as every Lp(a) seed in the book carries it: CMS Part B beneficiaries 6,779 in 2022 to 24,690 in 2023 to 48,298 in 2024. olpasiran.csv states why it cannot be less, that 'Leqvio's own 2023 to 2024 step of 1.96x is not reproduced by any midpoint below five at the k of 0.657 this seed already takes from that same series'
column12: slow on purpose: cardiovascular prevention is adopted slowly. Case for faster here than for the injectables: an oral taken once daily alongside an oral PCSK9 does not need a clinic visit, which is part of what makes Leqvio's ramp long

column11: the chain nvs_dii235.csv states for the book's other Phase 2 Lp(a) asset, run on this asset's own dates. Pelacarsen is the one Lp(a) programme that has run to an outcome: its Phase 2 (NCT03070782) reached actual primary completion 2018-07-26 and Lp(a)HORIZON (NCT04023552) reached actual primary completion 2026-07-16, 2,912 days later (registry, read 2026-11-10). MK-7262's Phase 2 (NCT07614984) has estimated primary completion 2027-10-12; 2,912 days on is 2035-10-02. With about six months to file, then 10 months from a filing date 60 days after receipt for a standard new molecule (data/fda_review_clock.csv, PDUFA VII commitment letter FY2023-2027), action falls around 2037-04 and 2038 is the first full year on sale

column12: an injectable anchor on an oral, which is the mismatch to argue with. MK-7262 is a once-daily tablet given with an oral PCSK9 inhibitor, where Leqvio is two administered injections a year, and an oral in a class with generic statins behind it usually prices below an administered agent. Against that, Leqvio's 2024 beneficiaries bought 6,650 dosage units between 2,681 of them, 2.48 each, so the figure is close to a full year of its own schedule rather than a part year. CMS Part D spending is gross of rebates and the next row takes it to net. No price for MK-7262 exists, and none exists for any Lp(a) drug
